A1.justification: Both complete 27-page PDFs describe RLZero and contain readable methods, experiments, mathematical material, references, and appendices. Renamed, renumbered, and relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on 25 language-control tasks and 10 cross-embodiment videos, together with discriminator and imagination-free ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds GenRL comparisons, distribution-matching returns, and seven HumEnv video-imitation tasks.

M1.justification: The imagine-project-imitate procedure, SigLIP retrieval, discriminator-free BFM inference, and imagination-free variant are retained. InternVideo2 was already specified in v1's appendix. The pretrained HumEnv BFM extends evaluation of the existing framework without establishing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds HumEnv/SMPL 3D humanoid control and seven cross-embodiment video tasks, substantially extending embodiment and task coverage. The original 25 language-control tasks and 10 Stickman video tasks remain.

E2.justification: GenRL becomes an evaluated model-based comparator across the language-control benchmark in v2 Table 1, substantially extending comparison beyond the previous reward-based offline RL baselines. In v1, GenRL supplied video-model components but was not evaluated as a baseline. TD3/IQL reward variants and SMODICE remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds quantitative evaluation using returns under a learned distribution-ratio reward for language and cross-embodiment imitation. The previous cosine-similarity evaluation remains in Appendix C.6. The added HumEnv experiments use a pretrained MoCap-based BFM and a 300-step horizon, introducing a distinct evaluation configuration.

E4.justification: The discriminator versus discriminator-free and imagination-free ablations retain identical numerical results. The imagination and retrieval failure analyses and examples are retained. The embedding-similarity analysis moves to Appendix C.6 rather than constituting a new supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 introduces Mann-Whitney U tests at significance level 0.05 and marks significant distribution-matching returns. Five-seed evaluations and reporting values with uncertainty already appeared in v1; no increase in repeated-run counts is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds GenRL's 76.8% win rate against the common TD3 reference, distribution-matching returns, runtime figures, and HumEnv results with 100% wins against SMODICE. RLZero's original 83.2% language-task win rate is unchanged. The original cosine scores and ablation tables are numerically retained, so the new return values do not establish a same-metric performance increase.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces v1's explicit successor-feature lemma and pretraining/greedy-policy formulation with a reward-regression objective and covariance-inverse solution in v2 Equation 2. This revises the formal background treatment; Theorem 1 and its Appendix A proof remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: v2 qualifies the headline claim from 'without any supervision' to 'without in-domain supervision' and explicitly claims quantitative as well as qualitative improvement over baselines. The central three-stage framework, direct policy inference, and absence of test-time policy training remain the principal contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning distribution-matching performance, policy reuse, and retrieval as the runtime bottleneck. It removes the explicit warning about temporal-order ambiguity in state-only matching and the future-directions discussion of representation and data-coverage limits. The imagination, retrieval, and cosine-metric limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds NVIDIA A40/AMD EPYC hardware information, policy-generation timing, the pretrained humanoid BFM source, and additional video prompts and sources. Core FB hyperparameters remain unchanged. Both judge-code examples omit the previously explicit temperature=0 setting, reducing that aspect of reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially repositions RLZero against video-conditioned control and video/language planning, adding discussions of text-guided video policies, Video Language Planning, Vid2Robot, RoboCLIP, and diffusion-based approaches. The revised distinctions emphasize executable closed-loop policies, in-domain supervision, and test-time training requirements.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, method exposition, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. The three method stages receive parallel subsections, the future-directions paragraph is removed, and appendix organization is revised. These changes extend well beyond terminology and citation-style editing.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, expands the main comparison table, adds cross-embodiment result displays, and extends the cross-embodiment illustration with humanoid examples. Algorithm 1 and existing visualization material move to the appendices; v1 Table 1 is retained as v2 Table 8 with a substantially different placement and scale.

improvement.justification: The GenRL comparison addresses an important missing comparator, while distribution-matching evaluations and significance tests substantially strengthen quantitative imitation evidence beyond v1's acknowledged-unreliable cosine metric. The 3D humanoid experiments provide stronger support for transfer. These gains outweigh the reduced limitation discussion, although the new returns remain proxies for agreement with projected demonstrations rather than independent measures of task success.
